# TreeView

Header: `winui/ui/collections/TreeView.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/collections/TreeView.hpp`.

A hierarchy of expandable rows, with single or multiple (check box) selection, templated rows, and rearranging by drag and drop.

The nodes are plain [TreeNode](#struct-treenode) data, set with [set_roots()](#set_roots). The rows are the visible nodes in order, and the tree draws each row's chrome itself: backplate, selection indicator, indentation and chevron. Which nodes are expanded and selected is kept by each node's key, so [set_roots()](#set_roots) with a changed tree keeps them. The tree is a single [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) stop. Up and Down move between rows. Left and Right collapse, expand, or step to the parent or the first child. Enter invokes. With [set_can_drag_items()](#set_can_drag_items) and [set_allow_drop()](../tree/element.md#set_allow_drop) on, a row can be dragged onto another row to become its last child, or into the gap between rows to reorder. [on_drag_items_completed()](#on_drag_items_completed) reports the move. The tree is not virtualized. Every visible row is realized, so keep very large trees collapsed.

Example: 
```cpp
auto tree = std::make_unique<ui::TreeViewControl>();
tree->set_roots({{.text = "Documents", .children = {{.text = "Report.docx"}}, .expanded = true},
                 {.text = "Network", .has_children = true}});
tree->on_expanding([raw = tree.get()](const ui::TreeNode& node) {
    if (node.text == "Network" && node.children.empty())
    {
        std::vector<ui::TreeNode> roots = raw->roots();
        roots[1].children.push_back({.text = "Server01"}); // load lazily
        raw->set_roots(std::move(roots));                 // the node goes on expanding
    }
});
// Enter or double-click:
tree->on_item_invoked([](const ui::TreeNode& node) { std::println("open {}", node.text); });
```

## `ui::TreeView`

A hierarchy of expandable rows over the app's data. Builds a [ui::TreeViewControl](#uitreeviewcontrol).

[`.items`](#uitreeview-items) are the top-level items, and [`.children`](#uitreeview-children) says where an item's children are: a member (`&Folder::subfolders`) or a function returning them. The data is the model. The tree shows it and keeps only which rows are expanded and selected, by [`.key`](#uitreeview-key), so that state survives a changed collection, such as a reload, a rename or children loaded on expand. A function [`.children`](#uitreeview-children) can make an item's children as they are needed, and [`.has_children`](#uitreeview-has_children) shows the chevron before they exist. [`on_expanding`](#uitreeview-on_expanding) loads them into the bound property, and the row opens.

With a member [`.children`](#uitreeview-children) and a bound [`ui::Property`](../core/property.md), a drag (with [`can_drag_items`](#uitreeview-can_drag_items) and [`allow_drop`](#uitreeview-allow_drop)) writes the rearranged items back.

The ready-made item is [ui::TreeNode](#struct-treenode), which needs no [`.children`](#uitreeview-children), [`.key`](#uitreeview-key) or [`.item`](#uitreeview-item). An item type of its own needs [`.item`](#uitreeview-item), the row's content. Name the item type as for the other views, [`ui::TreeView<Folder>`](#uitreeview). A braced list of [ui::TreeNode](#struct-treenode) works with a plain [`ui::TreeView`](#uitreeview).

Example: 
```cpp
struct Folder
{
    std::string         path;
    std::string         name;
    bool                has_subfolders = false;
    std::vector<Folder> subfolders;
    friend bool operator==(const Folder&, const Folder&) = default;
};
ui::Property<std::vector<Folder>> folders{{{"C:/", "Local Disk (C:)", true}, {"D:/", "Data (D:)", true}}};

window.set_content(ui::TreeView<Folder>{
    .items        = folders,
    .children     = &Folder::subfolders,
    .key          = &Folder::path,
    .has_children = &Folder::has_subfolders,
    .on_expanding = [&](const Folder& f) {
        std::vector<Folder> drives = folders.get(); // load the drive's folders lazily
        for (Folder& drive : drives)
            if (drive.path == f.path && drive.subfolders.empty())
                drive.subfolders = {{f.path + "Users", "Users"}, {f.path + "Windows", "Windows"}};
        folders = drives;
    },
    .item         = [](const Folder& f) -> ui::Spec { return ui::Text{.text = f.name}; },
});
```


## `ui::TreeViewControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ValueProvider`.

A hierarchy of expandable rows, with single or multiple (check box) selection, templated rows, and rearranging by drag and drop.

The nodes are plain [TreeNode](#struct-treenode) data, set with [set_roots()](#set_roots). The rows are the visible nodes in order, and the tree draws each row's chrome itself: backplate, selection indicator, indentation and chevron. Which nodes are expanded and selected is kept by each node's key, so [set_roots()](#set_roots) with a changed tree keeps them. The tree is a single [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) stop. Up and Down move between rows. Left and Right collapse, expand, or step to the parent or the first child. Enter invokes. With [set_can_drag_items()](#set_can_drag_items) and [set_allow_drop()](../tree/element.md#set_allow_drop) on, a row can be dragged onto another row to become its last child, or into the gap between rows to reorder. [on_drag_items_completed()](#on_drag_items_completed) reports the move. The tree is not virtualized. Every visible row is realized, so keep very large trees collapsed.

Example: 
```cpp
auto tree = std::make_unique<ui::TreeViewControl>();
tree->set_roots({{.text = "Documents", .children = {{.text = "Report.docx"}}, .expanded = true},
                 {.text = "Network", .has_children = true}});
tree->on_expanding([raw = tree.get()](const ui::TreeNode& node) {
    if (node.text == "Network" && node.children.empty())
    {
```

### ItemTemplate

```cpp
using ui::TreeViewControl::ItemTemplate = Callback<std::unique_ptr<Element>(const TreeNode&)>
```

Makes a row's content for a node and may choose a different look per node. Called during measure for each visible row. The result is kept per node until the tree changes.

### TreeViewControl

```cpp
TreeViewControl()
```

An empty, enabled tree in Single selection mode, with dragging and dropping off.

### set_roots

```cpp
void set_roots(std::vector<TreeNode> roots)
```

Replaces the tree. Nodes whose key was there before stay expanded and selected as they were. A new key takes its node's `expanded`. A selected node whose key is gone is deselected, which raises [on_selection_changed()](#on_selection_changed). Safe to call from [on_expanding()](#on_expanding), which is how children added on expand arrive. Invalidates every `TreeNode*` into the old tree and every row content the template made, and lays the tree out again.

### roots

```cpp
const std::vector<TreeNode>& roots() const
```

The top-level nodes, each owning its subtree, as last set or rearranged by a drag.

### find

```cpp
const TreeNode* find(std::string_view key) const
```

The node with `key`, or nullptr. A node without a key is found by its path of texts.

### key_of

```cpp
const std::string& key_of(const TreeNode& node) const
```

A node's effective key: its `key`, or the path of texts from its root.

### set_item_template

```cpp
void set_item_template(ItemTemplate item_template)
```

Sets the row content template. nullptr, the default, shows each node's text. Rebuilds every row's content on the next layout.


Whether `node`'s children show.

### set_expanded

```cpp
void set_expanded(std::string_view key, bool expanded)
```

Expands or collapses the node with `key`, as the chevron does, raising [on_expanding()](#on_expanding) first.

### selection_mode

```cpp
TreeViewSelectionMode selection_mode() const
```

The selection mode; Single by default.

```cpp

```

Switches the mode and adapts the selection. None clears it, Single keeps only the first selected node, and Multiple shows the check boxes. Lays the tree out again.

```cpp

```

The selected node, the first one in Multiple mode, or nullptr.

```cpp
std::vector<const TreeNode*> selected_nodes() const
```

Every fully selected node, in tree order.

### select

```cpp
void select(std::string_view key)
```

Selects the node with `key` alone, in Single mode. An unknown key clears the selection.

### selection_state

```cpp
TreeNodeSelectionState selection_state(const TreeNode& node) const
```

A node's state in Multiple mode. A leaf's is whether it is selected. A parent's follows its children: Selected when all are, Unselected when none are, else Partial.

### select_all

```cpp
void select_all()
```

Selects every node in Multiple mode, and does nothing in the other modes. Fires [on_selection_changed()](#on_selection_changed) once.

### on_selection_changed

```cpp
void on_selection_changed(Callback<void(const TreeNode*)> handler)
```

Fired whenever the selection changes, by a click, the arrow keys, a check box, or a selected key gone from [set_roots()](#set_roots). Called with [selected()](#selected): the selected node, the first one in Multiple mode, or nullptr when nothing is selected. Replaces any previous handler.

### on_item_click

```cpp
void on_item_click(Callback<void(const TreeNode&)> handler)
```

Called with the node on a single click on its row, before the click selects it. Not fired for a click on the chevron or check box.

### on_item_invoked

```cpp
void on_item_invoked(Callback<void(const TreeNode&)> handler)
```

Called when a row is opened: Enter or a double-click, and under TreeViewSelectionMode::None also a single click. Raised after the click selects. Not fired for a click on the chevron or check box.

### on_expanding

```cpp
void on_expanding(Callback<void(const TreeNode&)> handler)
```

A node is opening. Add the children of a node with `has_children` here, by setting a tree that has them ([set_roots()](#set_roots)). Fires before the node expands. If the node still has no children and no `has_children` afterwards, it stays collapsed.

### on_collapsed

```cpp
void on_collapsed(Callback<void(const TreeNode&)> handler)
```

Fired after a node has closed.

### can_drag_items

```cpp
bool can_drag_items() const
```

Whether rows can be dragged out to rearrange the tree; false by default. [Element](../tree/element.md)'s allow-drop flag, also off by default, decides whether the tree accepts drops. Rearranging the tree needs both.

### set_can_drag_items

```cpp
void set_can_drag_items(bool can)
```

Turns dragging rows on or off. Takes effect on the next press.

Called with the node that moved, at its new place, its new parent (nullptr for a root) and its position there. [roots()](#roots) already holds the rearranged tree.

A [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) stop only while enabled and non-empty.

### set_item_context_menu

```cpp
void set_item_context_menu(Callback<std::vector<MenuItem>(const TreeNode&)> menu)
```

Sets the context menu of a node. It is asked for on a right-click on its row, or on Shift+F10 or the Menu key while the node is the current one. The node is selected first, unless it already is or the selection mode is not Single. An empty list opens no menu. Replaces any previous one.

### raise_context_requested

```cpp
bool raise_context_requested(std::optional<Point> position) override
```

Offers a right-click first to the templated content of the row under `position`, then to the tree's own context flyout, and then opens the node's context menu.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

The node context menu while it shows, so the window finds its popup.

### drag_enter

```cpp
void drag_enter(const DragEventArgs& e) override
```

The drop events. [drag_over()](#drag_over) is asked first on the innermost drop target under the pointer, then on its drop targets up the tree until one accepts; every element asked has heard [drag_enter()](#drag_enter) first and hears [drag_leave()](#drag_leave) once the drag is no longer its business. The one that accepted gets [drop()](#drop). A control overrides them; the defaults run the handlers set with [on_drag_enter()](../tree/element.md#on_drag_enter)/on_drag_over()/on_drag_leave()/on_drop().

[drag_enter()](#drag_enter): the drag has come over this element; [drag_over()](#drag_over) follows at once.

### drag_over

```cpp
DragResponse drag_over(const DragEventArgs& e) override
```

The drag is over this element: answer what a drop here would do. Asked when it arrives and at every move. The default runs the [on_drag_over()](../tree/element.md#on_drag_over) handler, and refuses without one.

### drag_leave

```cpp
void drag_leave(const DragEventArgs& e) override
```

The drag left this element, was canceled over it, or was dropped on another target.

### drop

```cpp
void drop(const DragEventArgs& e) override
```

The pointer was released over this element while its [drag_over()](#drag_over) accepted. What the drop did is the operation it accepted.

### drag_completed

```cpp
void drag_completed(DataPackageOperation result) override
```

A drag this element started has ended. `result` is what the target did (None when the drag was canceled or dropped nowhere).

### automation_children

```cpp
void automation_children(std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

One accessibility item per root row. Each lists its content and its visible children.

### automation_parent_of

```cpp
Element* automation_parent_of(const Element& child) const override
```

A row's accessibility item is the parent of its content and of its child rows' items.

### automation_focus

```cpp
Element* automation_focus() const override
```

The row the keyboard is on, so a screen reader reads it as the arrow keys move.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Reported to screen readers as a Tree.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A pointer event for this element: the element under the pointer, one inside it that did not handle the event, or the element holding the capture. The position is in layout coordinates ([handle_pointer()](../tree/element.md#handle_pointer)). Return true when the event did something here, and it goes no further up; a handled press also captures the pointer until its release. A control that acts on a press (a click, a toggle, a caret placed, a drag started) returns true for the press and its release, so a list row or a card around it does not act on the same click. Default: false.

```cpp

```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).


Ticks the templated row content and drives the hover-to-expand timer during a drag.

```cpp

```

This element's own part of clear_dirty(): clear any part it owns but leaves out of [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) (a parked page, a hidden button), through that part's clear_dirty(). Default: nothing.

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### focus_changed

```cpp

```

Keyboard focus arrived (true) or left (false); [is_focused()](../tree/element.md#is_focused) already says so. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

A key for this element: the focused one, or one inside it that did not handle it. Return true when the key did something here, and it goes no further; false lets it bubble on to the parent and then to the shortcuts, a dialog's default button and arrow-key focus moves. Default: false.

```cpp
Rect focus_ring_rect(const Theme& theme) const override
```

Inside the row the keyboard is on. Around the whole tree when there is none.

### focus_ring_corner_radius

```cpp
float focus_ring_corner_radius(const Theme& theme) const override
```

The ring's corner radius: the theme's control radius by default.

### focus_ring_inside

```cpp
bool focus_ring_inside() const override
```

Whether the ring goes inside [focus_ring_rect()](#focus_ring_rect) in every era, its outer edge on the rect. False by default, which leaves it to the theme. An item inside a viewport (a list row, a tab, a menu item) returns true, as does a control in a tight spot, so a neighbor or the viewport edge never cuts its ring.

## struct TreeNode

A node of a tree: plain data, not an [Element](../tree/element.md). The ready-made item of a [ui::TreeView](#uitreeview), and what a [TreeViewControl](#uitreeviewcontrol) is given.

A tree keeps which nodes are expanded and selected by key. A new tree with the same keys, after a reload, a rename or children added on expand, keeps them. A node without a key is known by the path of texts from its root ("Documents/Report.docx").

Example: 
```cpp
ui::TreeView{
    .items = {
        {.text = "Documents", .children = {{.text = "Report.docx"}, {.text = "Budget.xlsx"}}, .expanded = true},
        {.text = "Music", .has_children = true}, // children added on expand
    },
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `std::string` |  | The row's label, and the name screen readers read for the node. Not displayed when an item template is set. |
| `key` | `std::string` |  | What the tree knows the node by. Empty uses the path of texts from its root. |
| `children` | `std::vector<TreeNode>` |  | The child nodes, in display order, owned by value. |
| `expanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the children show when the tree first sees this node's key. After that the user's expanding and collapsing count. |
| `has_children` | `bool` | `false` | Whether to show the chevron before the children exist. An on_expanding handler adds them. |

## struct TreeViewDragItemsCompletedArgs

What a [TreeViewControl](#uitreeviewcontrol)'s `on_drag_items_completed` gets: the node that moved, its new parent and its position there.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node` | `const TreeNode&` |  | The moved node, at its new place. |
| `new_parent` | `const TreeNode*` | `nullptr` | Its new parent; nullptr for a root. |
| `index` | `std::size_t` | `0` | Its position among the new parent's children (or the roots). |

## struct TreeViewMovedArgs

```cpp
template <typename T> struct TreeViewMovedArgs
```

What a [ui::TreeView](#uitreeview)'s `on_drag_items_completed` gets: the item that moved, its new parent (nullptr for a root) and its position among the new parent's children. Valid during the call.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | `const T&` |  | The moved item. |
| `new_parent` | `const T*` | `nullptr` | Its new parent; nullptr for a root. |
| `index` | `std::size_t` | `0` | Its position among the new parent's children (or the roots). |

## Enumerations

### TreeViewSelectionMode

```cpp
enum class TreeViewSelectionMode
```

How many nodes a [TreeView](#uitreeview) lets the user select.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | No selection. Clicks only invoke. |
| `Single` | One node, selected by a click or the arrow keys. The default. |
| `Multiple` | Any number, through a check box per row or Space. A click only invokes. |

### TreeNodeSelectionState

```cpp
enum class TreeNodeSelectionState
```

A node's selection state in Multiple mode, as its check box shows it.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Unselected` | Neither the node nor any descendant leaf is selected. |
| `Partial` | Some of the node's descendants are selected, not all. The check box shows indeterminate. |
| `Selected` | The node, or every descendant leaf, is selected. |
